messages:
Matt C: bringing up redwood-xl on an 8x H100 node (2 sockets). p95 looks ok but p99 has huge spikes only when NVLink is used across the two GPU islands. curious if this rings bells for anyone.

Yusuf: are you running with our default kernel heuristic? and what's your cpu/gpu affinity?

Matt C: default kernel (mode=auto) + pin_cpus=auto. microbench command:

Matt C: ```
./rwd_bench --model=redwood-xl --gpus=8 --seq_len=2048 --batch=1 --kernel=auto --affinity=auto
```

Olivia: auto can pick an NVLink global-KV strategy which shreds KV across all GPUs for lower median. but if threads drift across sockets you get rare global sync stalls.

Dan: can you paste tail numbers (p50/p95/p99) for NVLink vs forced-PCIE?

Matt C: NVLink path: 10ms / 43ms / 320ms

Matt C: Forced PCIE path (FORCE_PCIE=1): 13ms / 58ms / 95ms

Yusuf: huge p99 difference — NVLink helps median but triggers occasional huge stalls. probable causes: a) NUMA drift so DMA goes off-socket, b) OS scheduling pauses, c) long allreduce when a single GPU stalls.

Olivia: quick things to try: set socket-level NUMA pinning and prefer the local-KV kernel. example envs:

Olivia: ```
export RWD_AFFINITY=socket
export RWD_KERNEL_MODE=kv_local_first
export RWD_KV_WATCHDOG_MS=100  # fallback threshold
```

Matt C: ran with RWD_AFFINITY=socket + kv_local_first:

Matt C: NVLink (pinned, local-kv): 11ms / 46ms / 98ms

Olivia: that's promising — tail drops a lot. shows issue was cross-socket syncs during KV exchange.

Dan: can you test disabling peer-to-peer (simulate a PCIe-only fallback) but keep socket pinning, to compare throughput impact? we need a safe degraded mode for Dedicated servers.

Matt C: FORCE_PCIE=1 + affinity=socket:

Matt C: FORCE_PCIE (pinned): 14ms / 62ms / 110ms (throughput -12%)

Matt C: so a small hit on median/throughput but tails are bounded.

Erin: ops summary from bench: NVLink-global reduces median by ~20% but can cause rare KV stalls up to multiple 100s ms if CPU/GPU affinity not enforced. Recommended onboarding checklist: run a topology sweep (auto detect NVSwitch islands), test kernel modes (global-kv vs local-kv), record preferred kernel and affinity into model metadata, and enable KV watchdog with a fallback to PCIe path.

Matt C: filed ENG-ML #3501 with the harness changes: add onboarding sweep, store kernel hint in model manifest, and an automated test that asserts p99 < 120ms on 8-GPU nodes.

perf-bot: pushed latency histograms + kernel traces to https://internal/reports/bench/1771005566-charts (hist + flamegraphs).

Olivia: i'll add a short note to the docs and Console recommendations: "For multi-socket H100 nodes, prefer socket NUMA pinning + kv_local_first; enable KV watchdog to auto-fallback to PCIe when nvlink global-KV stalls exceed threshold."

infra-bot: rollout note: NUMA-aware onboarding sweep and kv_local_first default will be canaried to 10% of clusters at 02:00 UTC.

Matt C: thanks all, patching the onboarding harness now. :thumbsup:
